first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A company that helps you get married in Portugal and gives you one advisor to plan it. The top tells me straight away there's a month of legal process for foreigners and that some couples just do a symbolic ceremony there and marry legally at home. That's the stuff I actually came for. Then a big palace photo, which made me think 'this is for big fancy weddings' for a second.

attention_map.quote: Foreign couples start the legal process for a wedding in Portugal at least one month before the date.
attention_map.why: First thing that speaks to documents. I kept going because of this line, not the palace headline.

attention_map.section: Hero image and quick date checker
attention_map.why: Glad they ask guest count up front, but I can't see from the dropdown whether a tiny number like 6 is even an option. The 'Pena, Sintra' palace picture feels big-wedding.

attention_map.section: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue (palace and landscape cards, azulejo and fado images)
attention_map.quote: The legacy of Ferdinand II, the King-Artist
attention_map.why: History lesson about palaces. Nothing about how many people or what it costs. I scrolled fast through all of this.

attention_map.quote: whether you are planning an elopement, a small wedding or a three-day weekend
attention_map.why: First time I see the word elopement. And every region lists the nearest airport, which is exactly how I'd pick. 'Nearest airport: Lisbon (LIS)' is useful.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra
attention_map.why: Good to know but I'm not booking a palace for eight people.

attention_map.section: See Why Couples Marry in Portugal
attention_map.quote: A Legal Route for Foreign Couples
attention_map.why: Repeats things I've already read. The registry table image label caught me though.

attention_map.section: Pick the Setting for Your Ceremony
attention_map.quote: Catholic marriage is one of three recognised forms and is still registered through the civil registry.
attention_map.why: This answers my Catholic question directly. Also 'some estates have rooms for your closest guests' sounds like us.

attention_map.section: What Your Wedded Advisor Checks in Every Venue Contract
attention_map.quote: fees may be charged either way, with a minimum.
attention_map.why: So there ARE minimums, but they won't say what they are. That's the one number I scan for, and it's hidden. 'Exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill' also worries me with a small group.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding, Step by Step: Marrying Legally, by Passport
attention_map.quote: Witnesses are optional: two to four may take part.
attention_map.why: This is the best part of the page for me. Documents listed, translation rule, interpreter, witnesses optional, one month before, six months after. Official sources linked. I finally feel like I know where to start.

attention_map.section: What a Wedding in Portugal Costs
attention_map.quote: We talk you through the options for your plans.
attention_map.why: A cost section with no cost in it. Not even a starting figure for a small group.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package: every weekend is built to your plan.
attention_map.why: I wanted a small package. Instead it's welcome dinner, late party, Sunday brunch, a whole weekend. That's the big production I'm trying to avoid, though at least it says it's built around us.

attention_map.section: Bring Your Guests, or Keep It Exclusive to You / Celebrate More Than a Wedding
attention_map.quote: Some quintas have rooms for your closest guests
attention_map.why: Fine, but the anniversary, proposal and birthday cards are not for me.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding with One Wedded Advisor / How It Works
attention_map.quote: Your advisor talks you through your options: regions, venues, the legal route for your passport and what drives cost.
attention_map.why: One person for everything is what I want. But 'talks you through' is not the same as 'does the paperwork for you'.

attention_map.quote: Elopements and small weddings are welcome.
attention_map.why: This line sits right above the form, which is where I needed to see it. Form is long on a phone but it's dropdowns, fine.

attention_map.quote: Witnesses are optional in a Portuguese civil ceremony, so the two of you can marry with no guests at all
attention_map.why: FAQ 9 is literally my question. FAQ 3 answers Catholic. FAQ 4 on cost again says 'There is no single average'.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Feels like a gossip site at the bottom, and the 'Trending row' label looks unfinished.

questions_answered.question: Does this work for 30 guests or fewer, and is there a smaller package?
questions_answered.evidence: Small groups are clearly welcome ('Elopements and small weddings are welcome.', FAQ 9 'Can You Have a Small Wedding or Elopement in Portugal? Yes.'), but there is no smaller package: 'There is no set Portugal package'.

questions_answered.question: Do you handle the legal side: documents, witnesses, registry?
questions_answered.evidence: The legal steps are explained very well with official sources ('Gather your documents', 'Witnesses are optional', IRN, Smartraveller links). The advisor 'walk[s] you through the exact route to marry legally for your nationality'. It never says they lodge the documents or arrange witnesses for us.

questions_answered.question: What is the minimum spend?
questions_answered.evidence: 'fees may be charged either way, with a minimum.' and 'There is no single average: the cost depends on your guest count...'. No figure anywhere.

questions_answered.question: Can we have a religious ceremony (for example Catholic) here?
questions_answered.evidence: 'Yes for a Catholic ceremony: Catholic marriage is one of three legally recognised forms in Portugal, and it is valid once registered with the civil registry.'

objections_triggered.objection: Minimum guest numbers or spend that don't fit a small group
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'fees may be charged either way, with a minimum.' and 'Exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill'. Minimums exist but are only revealed after enquiring.
Mostly calmed by the 'Marrying Legally, by Passport' steps. Some worry left because the page explains rather than says 'we do it for you'.

objections_triggered.objection: Page feels pitched at big weddings
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Palace-heavy opening ('from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff'), three-day weekend list with 'A late party' and 'Sunday brunch'.

trust_signals_noticed: Clear legal steps with official sources: 'Legal and travel details from official sources, including IRN, GOV.UK and Smartraveller.' and 'checked October 2026'
Small-group welcome: 'Elopements and small weddings are welcome.'
Nearest airport listed for every region
Honest warnings: Monserrate roof works until 2027, state events can cancel palace bookings
One advisor as single contact: 'instead of one conversation per venue'
turn_offs_noticed: Minimums hidden until the call: 'with a minimum' but no amount
Opening section is palaces and history at a grand scale
Celebrity wedding links and a visible 'Trending row' label

images.stopped_me: registry-table-signing-portugal.jpg (a signing table is what my day actually looks like) and quinta-courtyard-dinner-table-portugal.jpg captioned 'some estates have rooms for your closest guests'.
images.felt_generic: azulejo-tile-wall-detail-portugal.jpg and fado-guitar-portugal.jpg feel like tourist brochure filler. Pena palace shots repeat three times.
images.missing: Nothing shows a couple alone or a tiny group of family. Every image is a place, a palace or a long table.

emotional_response.felt: Relieved by the legal section, a bit anxious about money.
emotional_response.intimate_and_personal: Partly. The words say small is welcome, the pictures and weekend list lean bigger.
emotional_response.overwhelmed: The page is very long on my phone. I had to dig past palaces to reach the bits about documents.

payload.decision_reason: Small weddings and elopements are clearly welcomed and the legal side is explained properly with official sources, and the advisor covers the legal route for my passport. That meets my bar. But I'm enquiring partly to find out the minimum, which the page admits exists and won't state, so if the first reply doesn't give me a number for about 10 people I'll drop it.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Honestly the legal bit is the best I've seen. Documents, witnesses optional, one month ahead, which embassy, all with links. And it actually says elopements are welcome. But it keeps talking about palaces and three-day weekends with late parties, and when I finally get to cost it says 'with a minimum' and then nothing. Just tell me the minimum. I'll fill in the form and put '10 guests, what is the minimum spend' in the box, because the form is right there and they asked my guest count anyway.
